source.observed_pattern: A MySQL query turns a grouped HAVING threshold into a scalar completeness flag by wrapping NOT EXISTS in IF, then reevaluates the flag after adding a member to an underfilled group.
source.mysql_mariadb_translation: Reauthored as an independent cohort audit. An inner join counts enrolled members for team cohorts, IF(NOT EXISTS(... HAVING COUNT(*) < 2), TRUE, FALSE) reports whether every represented team is complete, and a later enrollment changes the flag from false to true while a non-team cohort and an empty team remain outside the count. The source tables, identifiers, people, labels, and application workflow are new.

fixture_notes: Team cohort 20 starts with one enrollment and makes the initial completeness flag false; adding its second enrollment makes it true. Team cohort 40 has no enrollments and is ignored by the inner join, while non-team cohort 30 has one enrollment but is filtered out.
determinism_notes: Cohort and enrollment IDs are fixed, grouping uses the unique cohort ID, and every result read has explicit ordering; no clocks, randomness, sleeps, or concurrent schedules.
setup: CREATE TABLE cohorts (cohort_id INT PRIMARY KEY, cohort_name VARCHAR(32) NOT NULL, cohort_kind CHAR(1) NOT NULL)
CREATE TABLE enrollments (enrollment_id INT PRIMARY KEY, cohort_id INT NOT NULL, member_name VARCHAR(32) NOT NULL)

steps.sql: SELECT IF(NOT EXISTS (SELECT c.cohort_id FROM cohorts c INNER JOIN enrollments e ON e.cohort_id = c.cohort_id WHERE c.cohort_kind = 'T' GROUP BY c.cohort_id HAVING COUNT(*) < 2), TRUE, FALSE) AS all_teams_complete

SELECT IF(NOT EXISTS (SELECT c.cohort_id FROM cohorts c INNER JOIN enrollments e ON e.cohort_id = c.cohort_id WHERE c.cohort_kind = 'T' GROUP BY c.cohort_id HAVING COUNT(*) < 2), TRUE, FALSE) AS all_teams_complete

checks.sql: SELECT c.cohort_id, COUNT(e.enrollment_id) AS member_count FROM cohorts c LEFT JOIN enrollments e ON e.cohort_id = c.cohort_id GROUP BY c.cohort_id ORDER BY c.cohort_id
